dish: biang biang hand-pulled noodles; Bigguy stretch noodle soup; Shaanxi (Xi'an) cumin lamb
w: Despite the name it is Northwest Chinese: a Bethel Road strip-mall shop (since 2012) turning out fresh hand-stretched Shaanxi/Xi'an biang biang noodles slapped to order. Reviewed by Columbus Underground and named to The Infatuation's 24 Best Restaurants in Columbus guide. Google ~4.5 with high volume.

dish: mapo tofu with tongue-numbing peppercorns; Chongqing chicken; dry-pot cauliflower; dim sum
w: Boldly seasoned Sichuan and dim sum from Fortune's chef-owner Jiahe Weng and former Fortune staff. Named to Columbus Monthly's Best New Restaurants 2024 and reviewed by Columbus Underground ("Dim Sum, Adventure & General Tso's"). Yelp/Google high-rated with real volume.

dish: kamayan/boodle feast on banana leaves; lechon kawali; pork sisig; adobong ribs; lumpia
w: Columbus' first full-service Filipino restaurant (Grandview/Fifth-by-Northwest), leaning into pre-colonial Filipino tradition with weekly kamayan (Boodle) nights. Reviewed by Columbus Monthly, made its 10 Best Restaurants list (No. 10, 2022), covered by The Infatuation, and its kamayan documented by creator Breakfast With Nick.

dish: doro wat; kitfo; combination injera platters
w: The Ethiopian anchor that filled the hole left when Blue Nile closed — northeast-Columbus (Cleveland Ave/Cooke) spot open since 2014, praised by Columbus Underground and Columbus Monthly ("missing out on some of the best cuisine Columbus has to offer") and covered on alt.eats.columbus. Google ~4.5, strong volume.

dish: sambuus (samosa); Somali suqaar; hilib ari (goat); baasto pasta; jollof; clove-scented Afra iced tea
w: A build-your-own-bowl introduction to Somali food (Columbus has among the largest Somali communities in the US), on the Morse Rd corridor. Reviewed by both Columbus Monthly ("Somali flavors shine") and Columbus Underground, with a creator writeup from Breakfast With Nick. Restaurant Guru 4.8/845.

dish: grilled-chicken banh mi with house pate; pho; bun (rice vermicelli bowls)
w: Long-running Morse Rd Vietnamese room (murals, plastic fruit trees) singled out by Columbus Underground for a super-crunchy grilled-chicken banh mi and picked as a reviewers' favorite on alt.eats.columbus (Columbus Food Adventures). Google ~4.4 with high volume.

dish: shoyu-tonkotsu ramen; Meshikou Black (fireball miso ramen); karaage; BBQ chashu bun
w: Columbus' pioneering ramen shop (Bethel Centre), routinely called the best ramen in the city — and named best in Ohio by a national food guide. Columbus Monthly ran a First Look, and it's covered on alt.eats.columbus and by creator Breakfast With Nick. Yelp 587 reviews / Google high-rated.

dish: five-course sushi omakase; striped jack with Peruvian amarillo; torched sea bream with ponzu jelly
w: Columbus' first dedicated omakase counter (Polaris), from restaurateurs Jeff and Yenny Tsao — a $89+ set-menu tasting The Infatuation calls one of the most memorable dining experiences in Columbus, and named to Columbus Monthly's Best Restaurants 2025.

dish: green chickpea bhel with avocado & mango; Paan Clouds cocktail; progressive Indian small plates
w: "Progressive Indian" in the Short North — creative spins on traditional recipes with a strong bar. Reviewed by Columbus Underground ("Traditional Indian Meets Modern Sophistication"), featured by The Infatuation, and cited among Columbus Monthly's Best New Restaurants.

dish: from-scratch two-day pho broth (incl. vegan pho); banh mi; steamed egg-meatloaf topping
w: Fast-casual, build-your-own Clintonville pho shop whose broth is brewed two days before serving, with an unusually deep vegetarian/vegan/gluten-free menu. Opening covered by Columbus Underground and a Columbus Dispatch roundup. Google ~4.5.

dish: pollo al carbon (charcoal chicken); San Luis Potosi-style tacos; salsas
w: A decade-plus Columbus taco-truck institution famous for smoky charcoal pollo al carbon, which opened its first King-Lincoln storefront in 2024. On Experience Columbus' best-tacos guide and documented by creator Breakfast With Nick. (The old 1500 E Long truck lot shows closed on Yelp; the 695 E Long storefront is open.)

dish: jollof rice; suya steak; pounded-yam fufu; fried oxtail
w: Self-styled "most popular African food truck in the USA," made TikTok-viral by the fufu challenge and expanding to a brick-and-mortar at the Historic Trolley District's East Market (2026). Local expansion covered by NBC4; the viral rise documented by The Detroit News.

dish: Ghanaian jollof rice; waakye; peanut-butter (groundnut) soup; fufu; grilled tilapia
w: Northland Ghanaian restaurant from chef Lisa Bannerman, reviewed by Ohio Magazine and given a fresh Axios Columbus review (2025) praising jollof "comparable to Ghana," and long covered on alt.eats.columbus. Google ~4.6 with strong volume.

dish: cumin lamb; spicy twice-cooked fish; hot & sour fern-root noodles; pan-fried dumplings
w: University District specialist in Dongbei (Northeastern/Manchurian) Chinese cooking — a rare regional cuisine for the city, reviewed by Columbus Underground and Columbus Monthly ("Short Order") and written up by creator Breakfast With Nick. Google high-rated with real volume.
